intro.title: Lazy Loading Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a React application with multiple pages that loads efficiently by splitting your code into smaller bundles. You'll learn how to implement lazy loading using React's `lazy()` function and `Suspense` component to load components only when they're needed. This technique improves your app's initial load time by deferring the download of code for less frequently used routes. You'll work with React Router to define routes that load components dynamically when users navigate to them. By the end, you'll understand how to optimize large React applications by loading components on demand rather than all at once.
intro.usecase: Lazy loading routes is essential for large-scale applications like e-commerce platforms or SaaS dashboards where different sections (product listings, admin panels, user profiles) load independently. This pattern improves initial load times by only fetching code for the current view, such as when a user navigates from a homepage to a checkout page. Developers implement this to enhance performance in complex applications with multiple feature modules, ensuring users don't download unnecessary code upfront.
